items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: A trumpet player named Roy something -- I can't remember too well, but we went down there.

ctx.x: With different things -- it was I guess, sort of mystical, sort of mysterious, as long as it was in the black community. Now it affects so many people in so many different ways -- we did the same thing, for instance, with alcohol. You hadn't grown up until you smoked a cigarette and had a drink. Well, you had the same thing.

Same thing. When I first went to Quincy, Illinois, with the band -- not Flip's band, but this other band, Roy, I hadn't -- I mean, I would drink a little wine with the gang, because there were 10 of us on one pint, you know, and we'd swear we were high. But when I got to Quincy, they were serving it in these little pitchers -- whiskey -- and I didn't know nothing about drinking whiskey;

I was just sipping wine. So when we got upstairs, one of the guys says, "Do you drink?" "Yeah" -- I mean, I'm trying to be a man, and I wasn't but 15. "Okay, here, take a drink." And it was this little small pitcher; and he was pouring me a shot -- I picked up the pitcher and drank the whole pitcher.
